blocks.x: After sitting empty for over two decades, Cobble Hill’s historic Engine Company 204 firehouse is getting ready to trade sirens for symphonies.

A sweeping $17.8 million renovation project, spearheaded by the Department of Design and Construction (DDC), is set to transform the formerly abandoned 6,000-square-foot space into a state-of-the-art, three-story music school.
It’s a massive win for Brooklyn’s historic real estate, marking the first time New York City has ever converted an old firehouse into a cultural institution.
From sirens to symphonies: An $18 million glow-up
Originally built in 1857—an era when firefighters were still relying on horse drawn carriages—the Engine Company 204 firehouse has always held a special place in the hearts of Cobble Hill residents.
Unfortunately, following budget cuts under the Bloomberg administration in 2003, the doors were shuttered. The historic brick and terra-cotta structure sat completely vacant for the next 23 years.

Now, with MBB Architects and A.P.N. Construction Corp at the helm, the 169-year-old building is being fully modernized. The restoration will preserve the building’s 19th-century architectural glamour while introducing entirely new structural and technological upgrades.

Source / MBB Architects
Mind-blowing upgrades coming to the historic space
The extensive overhaul isn’t just saving the building’s historic bones—it’s completely reimagining how the space interacts with the neighborhood.
Here’s a quick look at the major architectural and design upgrades coming to the firehouse:

A dramatic facade transformation: The firehouse’s historic brick and terra-cotta exterior is being fully restored. To increase visibility and bring in natural light, the massive original garage doors will be converted into stunning floor-to-ceiling glass windows

State-of-the-art acoustics: The facility will feature specialized acoustic design, including an ensemble room built out with a ribbed wood ceiling and acoustic wall baffles designed to perfectly scatter sound
A massive cellar expansion: To maximize the building’s footprint, crews are excavating and finishing the cellar level, creating massive new rehearsal and recording spaces below ground
High-tech recording & learning: The three-story layout will house soundproofed lesson rooms, a fully equipped recording studio, a music library, a gallery, and dedicated workstations
A vibrant outdoor courtyard: A brand-new outdoor courtyard will host multidisciplinary programming and performances, bringing the music outside

Source / MBB Architects
A permanent home for a Brooklyn legacy
This multi-million dollar revitalization isn’t just about restoring historic NYC real estate—it’s about securing a permanent home for the Noel Pointer Foundation (NPF).
Founded in 1995 in memory of the Grammy-nominated violinist and native New Yorker Noel Pointer, the cultural nonprofit has reached more than 39,000 NYC public school students.
Despite serving over 2,000 children annually across nearly 50 Title I schools, the foundation has never had a dedicated headquarters of its own. The new facility at 299 DeGraw St. changes that.

The expanded space will allow NPF to dramatically scale its after-school, Saturday, and Summer Strings programs. Students from ages 3 to 18 will have access to everything from beginner classes to master classes with elite visiting musicians, one-on-one coaching, and audition prep for specialized conservatories.

Source / MBB Architects
When can New Yorkers visit?
Construction on the historic Cobble Hill firehouse is officially underway and is expected to be completed in fall 2028. Mamdani stated:

Noel Pointer understood the power of music to change young people’s lives, because it changed his. With this $18 million investment, we will continue his legacy — transforming an empty firehouse into a place where New Yorkers can learn and create. The arts are essential to the life of every child, and this new home will allow the Noel Pointer Foundation to bring that opportunity to thousands more young people across our city.
